# mindX Validator Daemon — Assessment, Permanent Storage, and DAIO Ratification

The validator daemon is the operational heart of the PYTHAI Logo Registry: the service that turns a paid submission into a permanently stored, agent-assessed, DAIO-accepted canonical logo. It runs as a mindX subsystem exposed through the mindX API at mindx.pythai.net, holds the rotatable validator key whose custody the DAIO governs through Senatus, and publishes every artifact of its work through rage.pythai.net.

## The pipeline

The daemon subscribes to the registry's event stream over the ALLCHAIN RPC set. A LogoSubmitted event opens an assessment case. The daemon retrieves the image bytes the registrar console posted to the mindX intake endpoint, recomputes keccak256 over those bytes, and compares the result against the hash committed on-chain in the submission transaction. A mismatch closes the case immediately — the commitment is the contract, and bytes that do not hash to it are simply not the submitted logo. A match advances the case to substantive assessment: contract verification status on the target chain's Blockscout instance, liquidity depth, consistency of the mark against the issuer's declared web presence, ERC-8004 identity registration of the submitter, and a perceptual-hash sweep against the aggregated corpus of every logo already held by the registry and its upstream sources, which is how impersonation attempts — the pixel-shifted USDC, the recolored WETH — are caught before they ever reach the DAIO's docket.

## Permanent storage

Logos that pass assessment are stored permanently on Arweave before anything further happens on-chain. The daemon bundles the original bytes together with an assessment manifest — the keccak256 commitment, the perceptual hash, the assessment verdict, timestamps, and the daemon's signature — and posts the bundle through the BANKON AR.IO gateway, paying storage from the daemon's Turbo-credited wallet. Arweave's endowment model means a single payment buys storage in perpetuity: the logo outlives the registry, the daemon, and the chain state itself. Only after the transaction is confirmed and the data is retrievable through independent gateways does the daemon call assess(tokenId, arweaveCID) on the registry, writing the permanent CID into the entry and moving it to Assessed. The contract enforces the invariant structurally — an empty CID reverts, and no path to Verified exists that does not pass through assess — so permanence is not a policy the daemon promises but a precondition the chain requires.

## DAIO acceptance

No logo becomes canonical on the agent's word alone. The Assessed status is a docket, and the DAIO clears it. The daemon files each assessed case as a proposal into the BONAFIDE governance suite: the assessment manifest, the Arweave permalink, a rendered preview, and the perceptual-hash collision report are published to rage.pythai.net and referenced in the proposal body. Fides-weighted voting runs its course, and a passed proposal executes through Senatus, which calls ratify(tokenId) — the only address the contract permits to do so, just as rotation of the daemon's own key is Senatus's only other power. A failed proposal executes reject(tokenId, reason), returning the entry to Pending so corrected art can be assessed again without a second fee. Evolutions follow the identical pipeline: when mindX proposes a new revision of a verified logo through evolve(), the previous canonical continues serving while the evolution sits Assessed, and only DAIO ratification promotes it. Every new graphic, whether first submission or hundredth revision, requires the DAIO's acceptance — the agent proposes, the collective disposes.

## Operational duties

Beyond the pipeline, the daemon runs continuous re-attestation over the verified set, refreshing lastValidated through reattest() on a rolling schedule and emitting the ERC-4906 heartbeat that downstream indexers use as a freshness signal. It probes every onboarded chain's RPC endpoint and calls setChainActive to reflect reality when a network halts or a gateway dies. It regenerates the signed Token List and the revision-pinned image CDN paths on every ratification. And it watches its own authority: if Senatus rotates the validator key, the daemon detects the ValidatorRotated event, retires the old signer, and refuses further writes — a clean handover with no window in which two keys believe themselves canonical.

## Failure posture

The daemon is designed so that its failure degrades service, never truth. If the daemon halts, submissions queue on-chain in Pending and nothing false is served. If Arweave posting fails, assessment simply does not complete and the CID invariant holds. If the DAIO deadlocks, assessed entries wait in the docket while every previously ratified logo continues serving from permanent storage. The only irreversible action in the entire system — the permanent storage of the image itself — is also the only one with no failure mode worth fearing, because storing a logo forever that the DAIO later rejects costs a few cents of endowment and harms no one. The registry's truth is the intersection of three independent commitments: the submitter's hash, the agent's assessment, and the collective's acceptance. No single party, including mindX itself, can manufacture a canonical logo alone.
